name: Pulihora (Andhra Tamarind Rice)
ingredients: Rice — 2 cups raw; turmeric — 1/2 tsp; salt — to taste; sesame/gingelly oil — 3 tbsp; tamarind — 1 large lemon-sized piece, soaked in hot water and strained; jaggery — 1 tsp, optional; chana dal — 1 tbsp; urad dal — 1 tbsp; mustard seeds — 1 tsp; cumin seeds — 1 tsp; dry red chillies — 3 to 4; green chillies — 4 to 5, slit; fresh curry leaves — 15 to 20; ginger — 1 1/2 tsp, finely chopped; asafoetida/hing — 1/4 tsp; roasted sesame-seed powder — 1 1/2 tbsp; roasted peanuts — about 2 handfuls.
procedure: 1) Wash 2 cups rice 2–3 times and cook it so the grains are fully cooked but remain separate; do not make the rice mushy. 2) Spread the cooked rice on a wide tray, gently separate the grains, add 1/2 tsp turmeric, a little salt and about 1 tbsp oil, then allow it to cool to room temperature. 3) Soak the tamarind in hot water, squeeze it well and strain to make a thick pulp. 4) Heat the remaining oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add mustard seeds and wait for them to crackle. 5) Add cumin, chana dal and urad dal; fry about 1 minute until the dals become light golden. 6) Add dry red chillies, green chillies, ginger, curry leaves and hing; fry briefly without burning the spices. 7) Add the tamarind pulp, jaggery if using, and salt. Cook on medium to low-medium heat for about 5–10 minutes, stirring regularly, until the raw tamarind smell reduces and the mixture becomes a thick but flowing paste. 8) Stir in roasted sesame powder and roasted peanuts, then switch off the heat. 9) Add the tamarind mixture gradually to the cooled rice and fold gently so the grains remain intact. Do not add all the paste at once. Taste and adjust salt or tamarind mixture. 10) Cover and rest for at least 1 hour; 2–3 hours gives stronger flavour development. Move to serving when the rice is evenly coated and the flavour has settled.
readyWhen: Rice grains remain separate; tamarind mixture is thickened and the raw tamarind smell has reduced.
mistakes: Overcooking rice; mixing while very hot; burning tempering; too much tamarind or fenugreek.
safety: Contains peanuts, sesame and mustard. Check hing packaging for wheat/gluten. Cool cooked rice promptly.

languages.en: Pulihora (Andhra Tamarind Rice). Beginner Cooking Mode: Cook rice until the grains are separate. Cool it completely before mixing. Make a tamarind seasoning by tempering mustard, cumin, chana dal, urad dal, chillies, ginger and curry leaves in oil. Add strained tamarind pulp, jaggery if desired and salt. Simmer until the raw tamarind smell disappears and the mixture thickens. Mix the seasoning gradually into the cooled rice, add roasted sesame powder and peanuts, then rest before serving.
languages.hi: पुलिहोरा (आंध्र इमली चावल)। शुरुआती कुकिंग मोड: चावल को इस तरह पकाएँ कि दाने अलग रहें। चावल को पूरी तरह ठंडा करें। तेल में राई, जीरा, चना दाल, उड़द दाल, सूखी लाल मिर्च, हरी मिर्च, अदरक और करी पत्ता तड़का दें। छानी हुई इमली का गाढ़ा पानी, चाहें तो थोड़ा गुड़ और नमक डालें। धीमी-मध्यम आँच पर तब तक पकाएँ जब तक इमली की कच्ची खुशबू कम न हो जाए और मिश्रण गाढ़ा न हो जाए। मिश्रण को धीरे-धीरे ठंडे चावल में मिलाएँ। भुना तिल पाउडर और मूंगफली डालें और परोसने से पहले कुछ समय ढककर रखें।
languages.ur: پُلی ہورا (آندھرا املی چاول)۔ ابتدائی کُکنگ موڈ: چاول اس طرح پکائیں کہ دانے الگ رہیں۔ چاول کو مکمل ٹھنڈا ہونے دیں۔ تیل میں رائی، زیرہ، چنا دال، اُڑد دال، خشک لال مرچ، ہری مرچ، ادرک اور کڑی پتے کا تڑکا دیں۔ چھانی ہوئی املی، حسبِ ضرورت تھوڑا گُڑ اور نمک شامل کریں۔ ہلکی درمیانی آنچ پر پکائیں یہاں تک کہ املی کی کچی خوشبو کم ہو جائے اور آمیزہ گاڑھا ہو جائے۔ آمیزہ آہستہ آہستہ ٹھنڈے چاول میں ملائیں۔ بھنا ہوا تل پاؤڈر اور مونگ پھلی شامل کریں اور پیش کرنے سے پہلے کچھ دیر ڈھانپ کر رکھیں۔
languages.ta: புளியோதரை (ஆந்திர புளி சாதம்). ஆரம்பநிலை சமையல் முறை: சாதம் உதிரியாக இருக்கும் வகையில் வேகவைக்கவும். சாதத்தை முழுமையாக ஆற விடவும். எண்ணெயில் கடுகு, சீரகம், கடலைப்பருப்பு, உளுத்தம்பருப்பு, காய்ந்த மிளகாய், பச்சை மிளகாய், இஞ்சி மற்றும் கறிவேப்பிலை தாளிக்கவும். வடிகட்டிய புளிக்கரைசல், விருப்பமிருந்தால் சிறிது வெல்லம் மற்றும் உப்பு சேர்க்கவும். பச்சைப் புளி வாசனை குறைந்து கலவை கெட்டியாகும் வரை மிதமான முதல் குறைந்த தீயில் வேகவைக்கவும். இந்தக் கலவையை ஆறிய சாதத்தில் மெதுவாகக் கலக்கவும். வறுத்த எள் பொடி மற்றும் வேர்க்கடலை சேர்த்து, பரிமாறுவதற்கு முன் சிறிது நேரம் மூடி வைக்கவும்.
languages.te: పులిహోర. ప్రారంభ వంట విధానం: అన్నం గింజలు విడివిడిగా ఉండేలా ఉడికించాలి. అన్నం పూర్తిగా చల్లారనివ్వాలి. నూనెలో ఆవాలు, జీలకర్ర, శనగపప్పు, మినప్పప్పు, ఎండు మిరపకాయలు, పచ్చిమిరపకాయలు, అల్లం, కరివేపాకు తాలింపు చేయాలి. వడకట్టిన చింతపండు రసం, కావాలంటే కొద్దిగా బెల్లం, ఉప్పు వేసి కలపాలి. పచ్చి చింతపండు వాసన తగ్గి మిశ్రమం చిక్కబడే వరకు మోస్తరు నుంచి తక్కువ మంటపై ఉడికించాలి. ఈ మిశ్రమాన్ని చల్లారిన అన్నంలో కొద్దికొద్దిగా కలపాలి. వేయించిన నువ్వుల పొడి, వేరుశెనగలు వేసి, వడ్డించే ముందు కొంతసేపు మూతపెట్టి ఉంచాలి.

name: Pesarattu
ingredients: Main ingredient named in the dish — 500 g; onion — 1 medium; tomato — 1 medium; ginger-garlic — 1 tbsp; oil — 2 tbsp; turmeric — 1/2 tsp; chilli powder — 1 tsp; salt — to taste; regional spice blend — 1–2 tsp; water — 200–300 ml.
procedure: 1) Prepare all ingredients for Pesarattu. 2) Heat a pan on medium for 30–60 seconds. 3) Add oil and whole spices. 4) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 5) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 6) Add tomato/spices and cook until thick. 7) Add the main ingredient and coat it. 8) Add water as required. 9) Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce to low-medium. 10) Cook until tender and the raw smell is gone, stirring every few minutes. 11) Taste and adjust. 12) Finish with the appropriate garnish.
readyWhen: The main ingredient is tender, the raw smell is gone, and the dish has the expected final consistency.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

name: Alasanda Vada
ingredients: Flour/grain base appropriate to the dish — 300 g; water — about 180–220 ml, added gradually; salt — 1 tsp; oil/ghee — 1 tbsp plus cooking fat as required.
procedure: 1) Put the flour/grain base for Alasanda Vada into a bowl. 2) Add salt. 3) Add water gradually until the correct soft dough or batter forms. 4) Rest 10–20 minutes if appropriate. 5) Heat a tawa/pan on medium for about 2 minutes. 6) Shape the dough/batter. 7) Cook until the surface changes colour and browned spots appear. 8) Turn and cook the other side. 9) Reduce to medium-low if it browns too quickly. 10) Remove when cooked through.

name: Rice Beer Rice Cakes
ingredients: Rice — 300 g; water — according to the chosen rice/method; oil or ghee — 2 tbsp; onion — 1 medium where appropriate; tomato — 1 medium where appropriate; ginger-garlic — 1 tbsp; turmeric — 1/2 tsp; salt — 1 1/2 tsp or to taste; regional spice blend — 1–2 tsp; vegetables or protein named in the dish — 300–400 g.
procedure: 1) Rinse rice and drain. 2) Prepare ingredients for Rice Beer Rice Cakes. 3) Heat a heavy pan on medium. 4) Add oil/ghee and whole spices. 5) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 6) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 7) Add vegetables/protein and cook until the outside changes colour. 8) Add powdered spices and salt. 9) Add rice and measured liquid. procedure: 1) Cut the main ingredient for Koldil Bhaji into even pieces. 2) Mix with salt, turmeric and spices. 3) Rest 10–20 minutes where appropriate. 4) Heat a wide pan on medium. 5) Add oil; it should be hot but not smoking. 6) Add pieces without crowding. 7) Cook 3–6 minutes, turn, and continue cooking. 8) Reduce to medium-low if the outside browns too quickly. 9) Cook through and drain excess oil.
readyWhen: The outside is evenly cooked/browned and the centre is fully cooked.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

name: Kharoli
ingredients: Main ingredient named in the dish — 500 g; onion — 1 medium; tomato — 1 medium; ginger-garlic — 1 tbsp; oil — 2 tbsp; turmeric — 1/2 tsp; chilli powder — 1 tsp; salt — to taste; regional spice blend — 1–2 tsp; water — 200–300 ml.
procedure: 1) Prepare all ingredients for Kharoli. 2) Heat a pan on medium for 30–60 seconds. 3) Add oil and whole spices. 4) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 5) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 6) Add tomato/spices and cook until thick. 7) Add the main ingredient and coat it. 8) Add water as required. 9) Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce to low-medium. 10) Cook until tender and the raw smell is gone, stirring every few minutes. 11) Taste and adjust. 12) Finish with the appropriate garnish.

name: Pitha Guri Pitha
ingredients: Flour/grain base appropriate to the dish — 300 g; water — about 180–220 ml, added gradually; salt — 1 tsp; oil/ghee — 1 tbsp plus cooking fat as required.
procedure: 1) Put the flour/grain base for Pitha Guri Pitha into a bowl. 2) Add salt. 3) Add water gradually until the correct soft dough or batter forms. 4) Rest 10–20 minutes if appropriate. 5) Heat a tawa/pan on medium for about 2 minutes. 6) Shape the dough/batter. 7) Cook until the surface changes colour and browned spots appear. 8) Turn and cook the other side. 9) Reduce to medium-low if it browns too quickly. 10) Remove when cooked through.

name: Narikolor Laru
ingredients: Main ingredient named in the dish — 500 g; onion — 1 medium; tomato — 1 medium; ginger-garlic — 1 tbsp; oil — 2 tbsp; turmeric — 1/2 tsp; chilli powder — 1 tsp; salt — to taste; regional spice blend — 1–2 tsp; water — 200–300 ml.
procedure: 1) Prepare all ingredients for Narikolor Laru. 2) Heat a pan on medium for 30–60 seconds. 3) Add oil and whole spices. 4) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 5) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 6) Add tomato/spices and cook until thick. 7) Add the main ingredient and coat it. 8) Add water as required. 9) Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce to low-medium. 10) Cook until tender and the raw smell is gone, stirring every few minutes. 11) Taste and adjust. 12) Finish with the appropriate garnish.

procedure: 1) Prepare all ingredients for Boror Tenga. 2) Heat a pan on medium for 30–60 seconds. 3) Add oil and whole spices. 4) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 5) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 6) Add tomato/spices and cook until thick. 7) Add the main ingredient and coat it. 8) Add water as required. 9) Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce to low-medium. 10) Cook until tender and the raw smell is gone, stirring every few minutes. 11) Taste and adjust. 12) Finish with the appropriate garnish.
readyWhen: The main ingredient is tender, the raw smell is gone, and the dish has the expected final consistency.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

procedure: 1) Prepare the protein for Pork with Lai Xaak in even pieces. 2) Heat a heavy pan on medium. 3) Add oil and whole spices. 4) Add onion and cook 5–7 minutes until golden. 5) Add ginger-garlic for 30–45 seconds. 6) Add tomatoes and powdered spices; cook 5–8 minutes until thick. 7) Add protein and coat thoroughly. 8) Cook 4–6 minutes. 9) Add water, bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to low-medium. 10) Cover and simmer until completely cooked. Poultry commonly takes about 20–30 minutes; mutton/goat may take much longer; fish/seafood usually takes less time. 11) Check doneness before serving. 12) Adjust seasoning.
readyWhen: The protein is completely cooked, tender as appropriate, and the sauce has the intended consistency.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

name: Makhana Kheer
ingredients: Main ingredient used in the named sweet — 500 g; sugar or jaggery — 125 g; milk or water as appropriate — 250 ml; ghee/oil — 1 tbsp; cardamom — 1/2 tsp; nuts/dried fruit — 30 g, optional; pinch of salt.
procedure: 1) Measure all ingredients before starting Makhana Kheer. 2) Prepare the main ingredient. 3) Heat a heavy pan on low-medium for 30–60 seconds. 4) Add ghee/oil and cook the main ingredient gently. 5) Add the liquid gradually and cook until tender. 6) Add sugar/jaggery and stir until dissolved. 7) Continue on low heat until the mixture reaches the intended consistency; do not use high heat. 8) Add cardamom and nuts near the end. 9) Switch off the heat and cool as appropriate.

name: Mutton Korma
ingredients: Chicken/mutton/fish/seafood/egg appropriate to the dish — 500 g; onion — 2 medium; tomato — 2 medium; ginger-garlic — 1 1/2 tbsp; oil — 3 tbsp; turmeric — 1/2 tsp; chilli powder — 1–2 tsp; coriander powder — 1 1/2 tsp; salt — 1 1/2 tsp or to taste; regional spice blend — 1–2 tsp; water — 250–400 ml.
procedure: 1) Prepare the protein for Mutton Korma in even pieces. 2) Heat a heavy pan on medium. 3) Add oil and whole spices. 4) Add onion and cook 5–7 minutes until golden. 5) Add ginger-garlic for 30–45 seconds. 6) Add tomatoes and powdered spices; cook 5–8 minutes until thick. 7) Add protein and coat thoroughly. 8) Cook 4–6 minutes. 9) Add water, bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to low-medium. 10) Cover and simmer until completely cooked. Poultry commonly takes about 20–30 minutes; mutton/goat may take much longer; fish/seafood usually takes less time. 11) Check doneness before serving. 12) Adjust seasoning.
readyWhen: The protein is completely cooked, tender as appropriate, and the sauce has the intended consistency.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

name: Fish Fry
ingredients: Main ingredient — 500 g; oil — 3–4 tbsp for shallow frying or enough for the chosen method; ginger-garlic — 1 tbsp; turmeric — 1/2 tsp; chilli powder — 1 tsp; salt — 1 1/2 tsp or to taste; regional spice blend — 1–2 tsp; souring ingredient where appropriate — 1–2 tbsp.
procedure: 1) Cut the main ingredient for Fish Fry into even pieces. 2) Mix with salt, turmeric and spices. 3) Rest 10–20 minutes where appropriate. 4) Heat a wide pan on medium. 5) Add oil; it should be hot but not smoking. 6) Add pieces without crowding. 7) Cook 3–6 minutes, turn, and continue cooking. 8) Reduce to medium-low if the outside browns too quickly. 9) Cook through and drain excess oil.

name: Machhli Bhaat
ingredients: Rice — 300 g; water — according to the chosen rice/method; oil or ghee — 2 tbsp; onion — 1 medium where appropriate; tomato — 1 medium where appropriate; ginger-garlic — 1 tbsp; turmeric — 1/2 tsp; salt — 1 1/2 tsp or to taste; regional spice blend — 1–2 tsp; vegetables or protein named in the dish — 300–400 g.
procedure: 1) Rinse rice and drain. 2) Prepare ingredients for Machhli Bhaat. 3) Heat a heavy pan on medium. 4) Add oil/ghee and whole spices. 5) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 6) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 7) Add vegetables/protein and cook until the outside changes colour. 8) Add powdered spices and salt. 9) Add rice and measured liquid. Bring to a controlled boil. 10) Reduce to low, cover and cook until tender. 11) Switch off and rest covered 5–10 minutes. 12) Fluff gently.
readyWhen: Rice is tender and the cooking liquid is absorbed; vegetables or protein are fully cooked.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

name: Pork Vindaloo with Rice
ingredients: Rice — 300 g; water — according to the chosen rice/method; oil or ghee — 2 tbsp; onion — 1 medium where appropriate; tomato — 1 medium where appropriate; ginger-garlic — 1 tbsp; turmeric — 1/2 tsp; salt — 1 1/2 tsp or to taste; regional spice blend — 1–2 tsp; vegetables or protein named in the dish — 300–400 g.
procedure: 1) Rinse rice and drain. 2) Prepare ingredients for Pork Vindaloo with Rice. 3) Heat a heavy pan on medium. 4) Add oil/ghee and whole spices. 5) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 6) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 7) Add vegetables/protein and cook until the outside changes colour. 8) Add powdered spices and salt. 9) Add rice and measured liquid. Bring to a controlled boil. 10) Reduce to low, cover and cook until tender. 11) Switch off and rest covered 5–10 minutes. 12) Fluff gently.
readyWhen: Rice is tender and the cooking liquid is absorbed; vegetables or protein are fully cooked.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

name: Khichdi
ingredients: Rice — 300 g; water — according to the chosen rice/method; oil or ghee — 2 tbsp; onion — 1 medium where appropriate; tomato — 1 medium where appropriate; ginger-garlic — 1 tbsp; turmeric — 1/2 tsp; salt — 1 1/2 tsp or to taste; regional spice blend — 1–2 tsp; vegetables or protein named in the dish — 300–400 g.
procedure: 1) Rinse rice and drain. 2) Prepare ingredients for Khichdi. 3) Heat a heavy pan on medium. 4) Add oil/ghee and whole spices. 5) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 6) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 7) Add vegetables/protein and cook until the outside changes colour. 8) Add powdered spices and salt. 9) Add rice and measured liquid. Bring to a controlled boil. 10) Reduce to low, cover and cook until tender. 11) Switch off and rest covered 5–10 minutes. 12) Fluff gently.

safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

procedure: 1) Cut the main ingredient for Lilva Kachori into even pieces. 2) Mix with salt, turmeric and spices. 3) Rest 10–20 minutes where appropriate. 4) Heat a wide pan on medium. 5) Add oil; it should be hot but not smoking. 6) Add pieces without crowding. 7) Cook 3–6 minutes, turn, and continue cooking. 8) Reduce to medium-low if the outside browns too quickly. 9) Cook through and drain excess oil.
readyWhen: The outside is evenly cooked/browned and the centre is fully cooked.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

name: Bhura Ghee Roti
ingredients: Flour/grain base appropriate to the dish — 300 g; water — about 180–220 ml, added gradually; salt — 1 tsp; oil/ghee — 1 tbsp plus cooking fat as required.
procedure: 1) Put the flour/grain base for Bhura Ghee Roti into a bowl. 2) Add salt. 3) Add water gradually until the correct soft dough or batter forms. 4) Rest 10–20 minutes if appropriate. 5) Heat a tawa/pan on medium for about 2 minutes. 6) Shape the dough/batter. 7) Cook until the surface changes colour and browned spots appear. 8) Turn and cook the other side. 9) Reduce to medium-low if it browns too quickly. 10) Remove when cooked through.

name: Meetha Bhaat
ingredients: Rice — 300 g; water — according to the chosen rice/method; oil or ghee — 2 tbsp; onion — 1 medium where appropriate; tomato — 1 medium where appropriate; ginger-garlic — 1 tbsp; turmeric — 1/2 tsp; salt — 1 1/2 tsp or to taste; regional spice blend — 1–2 tsp; vegetables or protein named in the dish — 300–400 g.
procedure: 1) Rinse rice and drain. 2) Prepare ingredients for Meetha Bhaat. 3) Heat a heavy pan on medium. 4) Add oil/ghee and whole spices. 5) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 6) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 7) Add vegetables/protein and cook until the outside changes colour. 8) Add powdered spices and salt. 9) Add rice and measured liquid. name: Ragi Roti
ingredients: Flour/grain base appropriate to the dish — 300 g; water — about 180–220 ml, added gradually; salt — 1 tsp; oil/ghee — 1 tbsp plus cooking fat as required.
procedure: 1) Put the flour/grain base for Ragi Roti into a bowl. 2) Add salt. 3) Add water gradually until the correct soft dough or batter forms. 4) Rest 10–20 minutes if appropriate. 5) Heat a tawa/pan on medium for about 2 minutes. 6) Shape the dough/batter. 7) Cook until the surface changes colour and browned spots appear. 8) Turn and cook the other side. 9) Reduce to medium-low if it browns too quickly. 10) Remove when cooked through.

name: Chana Dal Pitha
ingredients: Flour/grain base appropriate to the dish — 300 g; water — about 180–220 ml, added gradually; salt — 1 tsp; oil/ghee — 1 tbsp plus cooking fat as required.
procedure: 1) Put the flour/grain base for Chana Dal Pitha into a bowl. 2) Add salt. 3) Add water gradually until the correct soft dough or batter forms. 4) Rest 10–20 minutes if appropriate. 5) Heat a tawa/pan on medium for about 2 minutes. 6) Shape the dough/batter. 7) Cook until the surface changes colour and browned spots appear. 8) Turn and cook the other side. 9) Reduce to medium-low if it browns too quickly. 10) Remove when cooked through.

procedure: 1) Prepare all ingredients for Chawal Chilka. 2) Heat a pan on medium for 30–60 seconds. 3) Add oil and whole spices. 4) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 5) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 6) Add tomato/spices and cook until thick. 7) Add the main ingredient and coat it. 8) Add water as required. 9) Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce to low-medium. 10) Cook until tender and the raw smell is gone, stirring every few minutes. 11) Taste and adjust. 12) Finish with the appropriate garnish.
readyWhen: The main ingredient is tender, the raw smell is gone, and the dish has the expected final consistency.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

name: Unniyappam
ingredients: Flour/grain base appropriate to the dish — 300 g; water — about 180–220 ml, added gradually; salt — 1 tsp; oil/ghee — 1 tbsp plus cooking fat as required.

name: Sabudana Khichdi
ingredients: Rice — 300 g; water — according to the chosen rice/method; oil or ghee — 2 tbsp; onion — 1 medium where appropriate; tomato — 1 medium where appropriate; ginger-garlic — 1 tbsp; turmeric — 1/2 tsp; salt — 1 1/2 tsp or to taste; regional spice blend — 1–2 tsp; vegetables or protein named in the dish — 300–400 g.
procedure: 1) Rinse rice and drain. 2) Prepare ingredients for Sabudana Khichdi. 3) Heat a heavy pan on medium. 4) Add oil/ghee and whole spices. 5) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 6) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 7) Add vegetables/protein and cook until the outside changes colour. 8) Add powdered spices and salt. 9) Add rice and measured liquid. Bring to a controlled boil. 10) Reduce to low, cover and cook until tender. 11) Switch off and rest covered 5–10 minutes. 12) Fluff gently.

safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

name: Palak Poori
ingredients: Flour/grain base appropriate to the dish — 300 g; water — about 180–220 ml, added gradually; salt — 1 tsp; oil/ghee — 1 tbsp plus cooking fat as required.
procedure: 1) Put the flour/grain base for Palak Poori into a bowl. 2) Add salt. 3) Add water gradually until the correct soft dough or batter forms. 4) Rest 10–20 minutes if appropriate. 5) Heat a tawa/pan on medium for about 2 minutes. 6) Shape the dough/batter. 7) Cook until the surface changes colour and browned spots appear. 8) Turn and cook the other side. 9) Reduce to medium-low if it browns too quickly. 10) Remove when cooked through.

procedure: 1) Put the flour/grain base for Kolhapuri Mutton into a bowl. 2) Add salt. 3) Add water gradually until the correct soft dough or batter forms. 4) Rest 10–20 minutes if appropriate. 5) Heat a tawa/pan on medium for about 2 minutes. 6) Shape the dough/batter. 7) Cook until the surface changes colour and browned spots appear. 8) Turn and cook the other side. 9) Reduce to medium-low if it browns too quickly. 10) Remove when cooked through.
readyWhen: The centre is cooked through with no raw dough and the surface has the expected cooked/browned appearance.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

name: Pandhra Rassa
ingredients: Chicken/mutton/fish/seafood/egg appropriate to the dish — 500 g; onion — 2 medium; tomato — 2 medium; ginger-garlic — 1 1/2 tbsp; oil — 3 tbsp; turmeric — 1/2 tsp; chilli powder — 1–2 tsp; coriander powder — 1 1/2 tsp; salt — 1 1/2 tsp or to taste; regional spice blend — 1–2 tsp; water — 250–400 ml.
procedure: 1) Prepare the protein for Pandhra Rassa in even pieces. 2) Heat a heavy pan on medium. 3) Add oil and whole spices. 4) Add onion and cook 5–7 minutes until golden. 5) Add ginger-garlic for 30–45 seconds. 6) Add tomatoes and powdered spices; cook 5–8 minutes until thick. 7) Add protein and coat thoroughly. 8) Cook 4–6 minutes. 9) Add water, bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to low-medium. 10) Cover and simmer until completely cooked. Poultry commonly takes about 20–30 minutes; mutton/goat may take much longer; fish/seafood usually takes less time. 11) Check doneness before serving. 12) Adjust seasoning.

name: Kolhapuri Chicken
ingredients: Flour/grain base appropriate to the dish — 300 g; water — about 180–220 ml, added gradually; salt — 1 tsp; oil/ghee — 1 tbsp plus cooking fat as required.
procedure: 1) Put the flour/grain base for Kolhapuri Chicken into a bowl. 2) Add salt. 3) Add water gradually until the correct soft dough or batter forms. 4) Rest 10–20 minutes if appropriate. 5) Heat a tawa/pan on medium for about 2 minutes. 6) Shape the dough/batter. 7) Cook until the surface changes colour and browned spots appear. 8) Turn and cook the other side. 9) Reduce to medium-low if it browns too quickly. 10) Remove when cooked through.

procedure: 1) Cut the main ingredient for Vegetable Pakora into even pieces. 2) Mix with salt, turmeric and spices. 3) Rest 10–20 minutes where appropriate. 4) Heat a wide pan on medium. 5) Add oil; it should be hot but not smoking. 6) Add pieces without crowding. 7) Cook 3–6 minutes, turn, and continue cooking. 8) Reduce to medium-low if the outside browns too quickly. 9) Cook through and drain excess oil.
readyWhen: The outside is evenly cooked/browned and the centre is fully cooked.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

name: Lotus Stem Curry
ingredients: Main ingredient named in the dish — 500 g; onion — 1 medium; tomato — 1 medium; ginger-garlic — 1 tbsp; oil — 2 tbsp; turmeric — 1/2 tsp; chilli powder — 1 tsp; salt — to taste; regional spice blend — 1–2 tsp; water — 200–300 ml.
procedure: 1) Prepare all ingredients for Lotus Stem Curry. 2) Heat a pan on medium for 30–60 seconds. 3) Add oil and whole spices. 4) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 5) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 6) Add tomato/spices and cook until thick. 7) Add the main ingredient and coat it. 8) Add water as required. 9) Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce to low-medium. 10) Cook until tender and the raw smell is gone, stirring every few minutes. 11) Taste and adjust. 12) Finish with the appropriate garnish.

name: Pukhlein
ingredients: Main ingredient used in the named sweet — 500 g; sugar or jaggery — 125 g; milk or water as appropriate — 250 ml; ghee/oil — 1 tbsp; cardamom — 1/2 tsp; nuts/dried fruit — 30 g, optional; pinch of salt.
procedure: 1) Measure all ingredients before starting Pukhlein. 2) Prepare the main ingredient. 3) Heat a heavy pan on low-medium for 30–60 seconds. 4) Add ghee/oil and cook the main ingredient gently. 5) Add the liquid gradually and cook until tender. 6) Add sugar/jaggery and stir until dissolved. 7) Continue on low heat until the mixture reaches the intended consistency; do not use high heat. 8) Add cardamom and nuts near the end. 9) Switch off the heat and cool as appropriate.
readyWhen: The main ingredient is fully cooked and the sweet has the expected consistency.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

name: Jadoh rice vegetarian style
ingredients: Rice — 300 g; water — according to the chosen rice/method; oil or ghee — 2 tbsp; onion — 1 medium where appropriate; tomato — 1 medium where appropriate; ginger-garlic — 1 tbsp; turmeric — 1/2 tsp; salt — 1 1/2 tsp or to taste; regional spice blend — 1–2 tsp; vegetables or protein named in the dish — 300–400 g.
procedure: 1) Rinse rice and drain. 2) Prepare ingredients for Jadoh rice vegetarian style. 3) Heat a heavy pan on medium. 4) Add oil/ghee and whole spices. 5) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 6) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 7) Add vegetables/protein and cook until the outside changes colour. 8) Add powdered spices and salt. 9) Add rice and measured liquid. Bring to a controlled boil. 10) Reduce to low, cover and cook until tender. 11) Switch off and rest covered 5–10 minutes. 12) Fluff gently.
readyWhen: Rice is tender and the cooking liquid is absorbed; vegetables or protein are fully cooked.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

procedure: 1) Prepare all ingredients for Meghalaya Potato Curry. 2) Heat a pan on medium for 30–60 seconds. 3) Add oil and whole spices. 4) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 5) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 6) Add tomato/spices and cook until thick. 7) Add the main ingredient and coat it. 8) Add water as required. 9) Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce to low-medium. 10) Cook until tender and the raw smell is gone, stirring every few minutes. 11) Taste and adjust. 12) Finish with the appropriate garnish.

procedure: 1) Rinse rice and drain. 2) Prepare ingredients for Rice Porridge. 3) Heat a heavy pan on medium. 4) Add oil/ghee and whole spices. 5) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 6) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 7) Add vegetables/protein and cook until the outside changes colour. 8) Add powdered spices and salt. 9) Add rice and measured liquid. procedure: 1) Rinse rice and drain. 2) Prepare ingredients for Sticky Rice. 3) Heat a heavy pan on medium. 4) Add oil/ghee and whole spices. 5) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 6) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 7) Add vegetables/protein and cook until the outside changes colour. 8) Add powdered spices and salt. 9) Add rice and measured liquid. Bring to a controlled boil. 10) Reduce to low, cover and cook until tender. 11) Switch off and rest covered 5–10 minutes. 12) Fluff gently.
readyWhen: Rice is tender and the cooking liquid is absorbed; vegetables or protein are fully cooked.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

procedure: 1) Prepare all ingredients for Fermented Bamboo Shoot Curry. 2) Heat a pan on medium for 30–60 seconds. 3) Add oil and whole spices. 4) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 5) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 6) Add tomato/spices and cook until thick. 7) Add the main ingredient and coat it. 8) Add water as required. 9) Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce to low-medium. 10) Cook until tender and the raw smell is gone, stirring every few minutes. 11) Taste and adjust. 12) Finish with the appropriate garnish.
readyWhen: The main ingredient is tender, the raw smell is gone, and the dish has the expected final consistency.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

procedure: 1) Cut the main ingredient for Pork Fry into even pieces. 2) Mix with salt, turmeric and spices. 3) Rest 10–20 minutes where appropriate. 4) Heat a wide pan on medium. 5) Add oil; it should be hot but not smoking. 6) Add pieces without crowding. 7) Cook 3–6 minutes, turn, and continue cooking. 8) Reduce to medium-low if the outside browns too quickly. 9) Cook through and drain excess oil.
readyWhen: The outside is evenly cooked/browned and the centre is fully cooked.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

procedure: 1) Prepare the protein for Pigeon Curry in even pieces. 2) Heat a heavy pan on medium. 3) Add oil and whole spices. 4) Add onion and cook 5–7 minutes until golden. 5) Add ginger-garlic for 30–45 seconds. 6) Add tomatoes and powdered spices; cook 5–8 minutes until thick. 7) Add protein and coat thoroughly. 8) Cook 4–6 minutes. 9) Add water, bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to low-medium. 10) Cover and simmer until completely cooked. name: Pakhala Bhata
ingredients: Rice — 300 g; water — according to the chosen rice/method; oil or ghee — 2 tbsp; onion — 1 medium where appropriate; tomato — 1 medium where appropriate; ginger-garlic — 1 tbsp; turmeric — 1/2 tsp; salt — 1 1/2 tsp or to taste; regional spice blend — 1–2 tsp; vegetables or protein named in the dish — 300–400 g.
procedure: 1) Rinse rice and drain. 2) Prepare ingredients for Pakhala Bhata. 3) Heat a heavy pan on medium. 4) Add oil/ghee and whole spices. 5) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 6) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 7) Add vegetables/protein and cook until the outside changes colour. 8) Add powdered spices and salt. 9) Add rice and measured liquid. name: Chakuli Pitha
ingredients: Flour/grain base appropriate to the dish — 300 g; water — about 180–220 ml, added gradually; salt — 1 tsp; oil/ghee — 1 tbsp plus cooking fat as required.
procedure: 1) Put the flour/grain base for Chakuli Pitha into a bowl. 2) Add salt. 3) Add water gradually until the correct soft dough or batter forms. 4) Rest 10–20 minutes if appropriate. 5) Heat a tawa/pan on medium for about 2 minutes. 6) Shape the dough/batter. 7) Cook until the surface changes colour and browned spots appear. 8) Turn and cook the other side. 9) Reduce to medium-low if it browns too quickly. 10) Remove when cooked through.

name: Khaja
ingredients: Main ingredient used in the named sweet — 500 g; sugar or jaggery — 125 g; milk or water as appropriate — 250 ml; ghee/oil — 1 tbsp; cardamom — 1/2 tsp; nuts/dried fruit — 30 g, optional; pinch of salt.
procedure: 1) Measure all ingredients before starting Khaja. 2) Prepare the main ingredient. 3) Heat a heavy pan on low-medium for 30–60 seconds. 4) Add ghee/oil and cook the main ingredient gently. 5) Add the liquid gradually and cook until tender. 6) Add sugar/jaggery and stir until dissolved. 7) Continue on low heat until the mixture reaches the intended consistency; do not use high heat. 8) Add cardamom and nuts near the end. 9) Switch off the heat and cool as appropriate.
readyWhen: The main ingredient is fully cooked and the sweet has the expected consistency.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.

procedure: 1) Prepare the protein for Macha Tarkari in even pieces. 2) Heat a heavy pan on medium. 3) Add oil and whole spices. 4) Add onion and cook 5–7 minutes until golden. 5) Add ginger-garlic for 30–45 seconds. 6) Add tomatoes and powdered spices; cook 5–8 minutes until thick. 7) Add protein and coat thoroughly. 8) Cook 4–6 minutes. 9) Add water, bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to low-medium. 10) Cover and simmer until completely cooked. Poultry commonly takes about 20–30 minutes; mutton/goat may take much longer; fish/seafood usually takes less time. 11) Check doneness before serving. 12) Adjust seasoning.
readyWhen: The protein is completely cooked, tender as appropriate, and the sauce has the intended consistency.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

procedure: 1) Rinse rice and drain. 2) Prepare ingredients for Bajra Khichdi. 3) Heat a heavy pan on medium. 4) Add oil/ghee and whole spices. 5) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 6) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 7) Add vegetables/protein and cook until the outside changes colour. 8) Add powdered spices and salt. 9) Add rice and measured liquid. Bring to a controlled boil. 10) Reduce to low, cover and cook until tender. 11) Switch off and rest covered 5–10 minutes. 12) Fluff gently.
readyWhen: Rice is tender and the cooking liquid is absorbed; vegetables or protein are fully cooked.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

name: Methi Bajra Poori
ingredients: Flour/grain base appropriate to the dish — 300 g; water — about 180–220 ml, added gradually; salt — 1 tsp; oil/ghee — 1 tbsp plus cooking fat as required.
procedure: 1) Put the flour/grain base for Methi Bajra Poori into a bowl. 2) Add salt. 3) Add water gradually until the correct soft dough or batter forms. 4) Rest 10–20 minutes if appropriate. 5) Heat a tawa/pan on medium for about 2 minutes. 6) Shape the dough/batter. 7) Cook until the surface changes colour and browned spots appear. 8) Turn and cook the other side. 9) Reduce to medium-low if it browns too quickly. 10) Remove when cooked through.

Ready when: The main ingredient is fully cooked and the sweet has the expected consistency.

name: Raab
ingredients: Main ingredient named in the dish — 500 g; onion — 1 medium; tomato — 1 medium; ginger-garlic — 1 tbsp; oil — 2 tbsp; turmeric — 1/2 tsp; chilli powder — 1 tsp; salt — to taste; regional spice blend — 1–2 tsp; water — 200–300 ml.
procedure: 1) Prepare all ingredients for Raab. 2) Heat a pan on medium for 30–60 seconds. 3) Add oil and whole spices. 4) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 5) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 6) Add tomato/spices and cook until thick. 7) Add the main ingredient and coat it. 8) Add water as required. 9) Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce to low-medium. 10) Cook until tender and the raw smell is gone, stirring every few minutes. 11) Taste and adjust. 12) Finish with the appropriate garnish.
readyWhen: The main ingredient is tender, the raw smell is gone, and the dish has the expected final consistency.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

name: Sel Roti
ingredients: Flour/grain base appropriate to the dish — 300 g; water — about 180–220 ml, added gradually; salt — 1 tsp; oil/ghee — 1 tbsp plus cooking fat as required.
procedure: 1) Put the flour/grain base for Sel Roti into a bowl. 2) Add salt. 3) Add water gradually until the correct soft dough or batter forms. 4) Rest 10–20 minutes if appropriate. 5) Heat a tawa/pan on medium for about 2 minutes. 6) Shape the dough/batter. 7) Cook until the surface changes colour and browned spots appear. 8) Turn and cook the other side. 9) Reduce to medium-low if it browns too quickly. 10) Remove when cooked through.
readyWhen: The centre is cooked through with no raw dough and the surface has the expected cooked/browned appearance.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

procedure: 1) Prepare all ingredients for Potato Curry. 2) Heat a pan on medium for 30–60 seconds. 3) Add oil and whole spices. 4) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 5) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 6) Add tomato/spices and cook until thick. 7) Add the main ingredient and coat it. 8) Add water as required. 9) Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce to low-medium. 10) Cook until tender and the raw smell is gone, stirring every few minutes. 11) Taste and adjust. 12) Finish with the appropriate garnish.
readyWhen: The main ingredient is tender, the raw smell is gone, and the dish has the expected final consistency.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

name: Rice Porridge

procedure: 1) Rinse rice and drain. 2) Prepare ingredients for Rice Porridge. 3) Heat a heavy pan on medium. 4) Add oil/ghee and whole spices. 5) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 6) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 7) Add vegetables/protein and cook until the outside changes colour. 8) Add powdered spices and salt. 9) Add rice and measured liquid. ingredients: Main ingredient named in the dish — 500 g; onion — 1 medium; tomato — 1 medium; ginger-garlic — 1 tbsp; oil — 2 tbsp; turmeric — 1/2 tsp; chilli powder — 1 tsp; salt — to taste; regional spice blend — 1–2 tsp; water — 200–300 ml.
procedure: 1) Prepare all ingredients for Churpi Chutney. 2) Heat a pan on medium for 30–60 seconds. 3) Add oil and whole spices. 4) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 5) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 6) Add tomato/spices and cook until thick. 7) Add the main ingredient and coat it. 8) Add water as required. 9) Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce to low-medium. 10) Cook until tender and the raw smell is gone, stirring every few minutes. 11) Taste and adjust. 12) Finish with the appropriate garnish.

procedure: 1) Put the flour/grain base for Idli into a bowl. 2) Add salt. 3) Add water gradually until the correct soft dough or batter forms. 4) Rest 10–20 minutes if appropriate. 5) Heat a tawa/pan on medium for about 2 minutes. 6) Shape the dough/batter. 7) Cook until the surface changes colour and browned spots appear. 8) Turn and cook the other side. 9) Reduce to medium-low if it browns too quickly. 10) Remove when cooked through.
readyWhen: The centre is cooked through with no raw dough and the surface has the expected cooked/browned appearance.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

name: Adai
ingredients: Main ingredient named in the dish — 500 g; onion — 1 medium; tomato — 1 medium; ginger-garlic — 1 tbsp; oil — 2 tbsp; turmeric — 1/2 tsp; chilli powder — 1 tsp; salt — to taste; regional spice blend — 1–2 tsp; water — 200–300 ml.
procedure: 1) Prepare all ingredients for Adai. 2) Heat a pan on medium for 30–60 seconds. 3) Add oil and whole spices. 4) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 5) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 6) Add tomato/spices and cook until thick. 7) Add the main ingredient and coat it. 8) Add water as required. 9) Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce to low-medium. 10) Cook until tender and the raw smell is gone, stirring every few minutes. 11) Taste and adjust. 12) Finish with the appropriate garnish.

name: Pongal Sweet

procedure: 1) Rinse rice and drain. 2) Prepare ingredients for Pongal Sweet. 3) Heat a heavy pan on medium. 4) Add oil/ghee and whole spices. 5) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 6) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 7) Add vegetables/protein and cook until the outside changes colour. 8) Add powdered spices and salt. 9) Add rice and measured liquid. name: Dosakaya Pachadi
ingredients: Flour/grain base appropriate to the dish — 300 g; water — about 180–220 ml, added gradually; salt — 1 tsp; oil/ghee — 1 tbsp plus cooking fat as required.
procedure: 1) Put the flour/grain base for Dosakaya Pachadi into a bowl. 2) Add salt. 3) Add water gradually until the correct soft dough or batter forms. 4) Rest 10–20 minutes if appropriate. 5) Heat a tawa/pan on medium for about 2 minutes. 6) Shape the dough/batter. 7) Cook until the surface changes colour and browned spots appear. 8) Turn and cook the other side. 9) Reduce to medium-low if it browns too quickly. 10) Remove when cooked through.
readyWhen: The centre is cooked through with no raw dough and the surface has the expected cooked/browned appearance.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

name: Mui Borok Pork
ingredients: Chicken/mutton/fish/seafood/egg appropriate to the dish — 500 g; onion — 2 medium; tomato — 2 medium; ginger-garlic — 1 1/2 tbsp; oil — 3 tbsp; turmeric — 1/2 tsp; chilli powder — 1–2 tsp; coriander powder — 1 1/2 tsp; salt — 1 1/2 tsp or to taste; regional spice blend — 1–2 tsp; water — 250–400 ml.
procedure: 1) Prepare the protein for Mui Borok Pork in even pieces. 2) Heat a heavy pan on medium. 3) Add oil and whole spices. 4) Add onion and cook 5–7 minutes until golden. 5) Add ginger-garlic for 30–45 seconds. 6) Add tomatoes and powdered spices; cook 5–8 minutes until thick. 7) Add protein and coat thoroughly. 8) Cook 4–6 minutes. 9) Add water, bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to low-medium. 10) Cover and simmer until completely cooked. Poultry commonly takes about 20–30 minutes; mutton/goat may take much longer; fish/seafood usually takes less time. 11) Check doneness before serving. 12) Adjust seasoning.
readyWhen: The protein is completely cooked, tender as appropriate, and the sauce has the intended consistency.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

readyWhen: The protein is completely cooked, tender as appropriate, and the sauce has the intended consistency.

procedure: 1) Cut the main ingredient for Kadhi Pakora into even pieces. 2) Mix with salt, turmeric and spices. 3) Rest 10–20 minutes where appropriate. 4) Heat a wide pan on medium. 5) Add oil; it should be hot but not smoking. 6) Add pieces without crowding. 7) Cook 3–6 minutes, turn, and continue cooking. 8) Reduce to medium-low if the outside browns too quickly. 9) Cook through and drain excess oil.
readyWhen: The outside is evenly cooked/browned and the centre is fully cooked.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.
safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

name: Baingan Bharta
ingredients: Main ingredient named in the dish — 500 g; onion — 1 medium; tomato — 1 medium; ginger-garlic — 1 tbsp; oil — 2 tbsp; turmeric — 1/2 tsp; chilli powder — 1 tsp; salt — to taste; regional spice blend — 1–2 tsp; water — 200–300 ml.
procedure: 1) Prepare all ingredients for Baingan Bharta. 2) Heat a pan on medium for 30–60 seconds. 3) Add oil and whole spices. 4) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 5) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 6) Add tomato/spices and cook until thick. 7) Add the main ingredient and coat it. 8) Add water as required. 9) Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce to low-medium. 10) Cook until tender and the raw smell is gone, stirring every few minutes. 11) Taste and adjust. 12) Finish with the appropriate garnish.

procedure: 1) Rinse rice and drain. 2) Prepare ingredients for Biryani Lucknowi. 3) Heat a heavy pan on medium. 4) Add oil/ghee and whole spices. 5) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 6) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 7) Add vegetables/protein and cook until the outside changes colour. 8) Add powdered spices and salt. 9) Add rice and measured liquid. name: Bhaat
ingredients: Rice — 300 g; water — according to the chosen rice/method; oil or ghee — 2 tbsp; onion — 1 medium where appropriate; tomato — 1 medium where appropriate; ginger-garlic — 1 tbsp; turmeric — 1/2 tsp; salt — 1 1/2 tsp or to taste; regional spice blend — 1–2 tsp; vegetables or protein named in the dish — 300–400 g.
procedure: 1) Rinse rice and drain. 2) Prepare ingredients for Bhaat. 3) Heat a heavy pan on medium. 4) Add oil/ghee and whole spices. 5) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 6) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 7) Add vegetables/protein and cook until the outside changes colour. 8) Add powdered spices and salt. 9) Add rice and measured liquid. name: Ras Bhaat
ingredients: Rice — 300 g; water — according to the chosen rice/method; oil or ghee — 2 tbsp; onion — 1 medium where appropriate; tomato — 1 medium where appropriate; ginger-garlic — 1 tbsp; turmeric — 1/2 tsp; salt — 1 1/2 tsp or to taste; regional spice blend — 1–2 tsp; vegetables or protein named in the dish — 300–400 g.
procedure: 1) Rinse rice and drain. 2) Prepare ingredients for Ras Bhaat. 3) Heat a heavy pan on medium. 4) Add oil/ghee and whole spices. 5) Cook onion 4–6 minutes until softened. 6) Add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds. 7) Add vegetables/protein and cook until the outside changes colour. 8) Add powdered spices and salt. 9) Add rice and measured liquid. safety: Wash hands and utensils after raw protein. Cook meat, poultry, fish and eggs thoroughly. Potential allergens vary by recipe and may include dairy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame, mustard, gluten and shellfish.

readyWhen: The protein is completely cooked, tender as appropriate, and the sauce has the intended consistency.
mistakes: Do not use high heat throughout. Watch spices and onions closely. If food browns too fast, reduce heat. If a curry is watery, simmer uncovered; if too dry, add a little hot water.

procedure: 1) Prepare ingredients for Mutton Jhol. 2) Heat a pot on medium. 3) Add oil and cook onion 3–5 minutes. 4) Add ginger-garlic and spices for 30–45 seconds. 5) Add the main ingredient and stir 1–2 minutes. 6) Add water/stock and bring to a gentle boil. 7) Reduce to low-medium and simmer. 8) Stir every 4–5 minutes. 9) Cook until the main ingredient is tender and the broth is flavourful. 10) Add delicate herbs/souring ingredients near the end. 11) Taste and adjust.

name: Mutton Jhol

procedure: 1) Prepare ingredients for Mutton Jhol. 2) Heat a pot on medium. 3) Add oil and cook onion 3–5 minutes. 4) Add ginger-garlic and spices for 30–45 seconds. 5) Add the main ingredient and stir 1–2 minutes. 6) Add water/stock and bring to a gentle boil. 7) Reduce to low-medium and simmer. 8) Stir every 4–5 minutes. 9) Cook until the main ingredient is tender and the broth is flavourful. 10) Add delicate herbs/souring ingredients near the end. 11) Taste and adjust.

Poultry commonly takes about 20–30 minutes; mutton/goat may take much longer; fish/seafood usually takes less time. 11) Check doneness before serving. 12) Adjust seasoning. Ready when: The protein is completely cooked, tender as appropriate, and the sauce has the intended consistency.
